paper_metadata.title: Bermudan option pricing by quantum amplitude estimation and Chebyshev interpolation

summary: This paper proposes a theoretical Bermudan option pricing algorithm that combines quantum amplitude estimation with Chebyshev interpolation. The main asymptotic result is an oracle complexity of O(epsilon^-1 log^d(epsilon^-1) polyloglog(epsilon^-1)) versus O(epsilon^-2) for classical Monte Carlo/LSM, with a 0.99 success probability under the stated parameter choices.

experiments.description: Quantum Bermudan option pricing using Chebyshev interpolation with quantum amplitude estimation to estimate continuation values at interpolation nodes and the initial option value.

algorithm.variant: Quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) combined with Chebyshev interpolation for Bermudan option pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Underlying asset-price transition distribution is encoded in a quantum state via an oracle O_step,k; payoff/value is scaled into [0,1] and encoded into a single qubit via controlled rotation for QAE.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Bermudan option value V_0 = E[V_1(S_1)] with backward dynamic programming V_k(s)=max(f_pay_k(s), Q_k(s)), where Q_k(s)=E[V_{k+1}(S_{k+1})|S_k=s].
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No QUBO/penalty formulation; early exercise handled by max{payoff, continuation value}. Out-of-domain asset values handled by either known outside-bound approximation V_k^OB or flat extrapolation F_k[·].

problem_instance.description: General Bermudan option pricing with d underlying assets and K exercise dates; paper is algorithmic and does not report a specific market contract instance or numerical benchmark.

dataset_specification.description: No concrete dataset; underlying asset evolution is assumed given by a stochastic model and discretized transition oracle.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Not reported; assumes discretized time evolution and finite support for conditional next-step states in the oracle model.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical error and complexity analysis only; no numerical experiments reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Chebyshev interpolation and classical post-processing of QAE estimates
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct Chebyshev nodes on D_k; choose interpolation degree m_k; scale continuation values into [0,1] using eVmax_k.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute Chebyshev coefficients from QAE-estimated nodal values; backward recursion of option values; final rescaling from QAE probability to option value.

results.unit: oracle calls to classical Monte Carlo-based methods (e.g., LSM)
oracle calls to O_step,k for the full algorithm

results.value: eLambda_1,K-1 * epsilon_int_k + eLambda_1,K-1 * epsilon_OB_k + sum_k eLambda_1,k * epsilon_QAE_k

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical Monte Carlo-based methods such as least-squares Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming access to the transition oracle O_step,k and QAE subroutines; asymptotic in epsilon
speedup_claims.caveats: Full algorithm has additional log^d(epsilon^-1) polyloglog(epsilon^-1) factors; no numerical experiment is reported.
The paper notes the exponential-in-K factor in the error bound and that the bound may be pessimistic.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(epsilon^-1 log^d(epsilon^-1) polyloglog(epsilon^-1)) calls to the transition oracle O_step,k for the main algorithm; QAE subroutine uses O(epsilon^-1) oracle calls per estimate.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: LSM and related Monte Carlo-based methods scale as O(epsilon^-2) oracle calls in the high-smoothness limit; paper also cites more general LSM rate from the literature.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault-tolerant or at least large-scale logical quantum hardware capable of repeated QAE calls and state preparation for the transition oracle O_step,k; no concrete hardware resource estimate is given in the paper.
limiting_factors: No experimental implementation or hardware benchmark is reported
Complexity is only asymptotic in oracle calls, not end-to-end wall-clock time
Requires efficient state preparation / transition-oracle access for asset-price evolution
Quadratic speedup only, which Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis generally deems insufficient on near-term hardware
Error bound includes log^d(epsilon^-1) and polyloglog factors, plus an exponential-in-K factor in the pessimistic bound

notes: No concrete hardware or implementation benchmark is reported; the paper is purely theoretical.

num_qubits is not explicitly stated because the circuit size depends on the discretization of the asset-state register, the QAE construction, and the chosen interpolation grid; only the abstract oracle/state structure is given.
Circuit depth is not numerically specified; only asymptotic oracle-call complexity is analyzed.
The paper is purely theoretical and reports no numerical experiments or device runs.
It claims a quadratic speedup in oracle calls versus classical Monte Carlo/LSM, but does not demonstrate practical advantage on hardware.
